paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: knowing the real Jesus protects you from a fake one. Paul is jealous for the Corinthians with a godly jealousy, because he promised them to one husband, Christ (2 Corinthians 11:2). He's afraid their minds could be "led astray from your simple and pure devotion to Christ" (2 Corinthians 11:3). The danger isn't a loud villain kicking down the door, it's a different Jesus, a different spirit or a different gospel sliding in so easy you barely notice (2 Corinthians 11:4).

Now here's the part that keeps a baker sharp. Paul says false apostles are "masquerading as apostles of Christ," and no wonder, because "Satan himself masquerades as an angel of light" (2 Corinthians 11:13-14). So a counterfeit can look shiny, sound impressive and use all the right words. That's why you can't judge by the packaging, friend. You check it against what you've already been given, and the more of God's Word you've got in you, the quicker you spot the knockoff. And Paul says their end will match their actions (2 Corinthians 11:15), so the disguise doesn't last.

Paul also shows what the real thing looks like. He preached God's gospel free of charge, and he wouldn't be a burden to them (2 Corinthians 11:7-9). When he asks, "Because I do not love you?" he answers, "God knows I do!" (2 Corinthians 11:11). I think that's the heart under all of it: someone who loves you wants you close to Christ, not close to them. So stay in the Word, baker, keep your devotion simple and pure, and let the real Jesus be the one you know by heart.
